## Redo causes and termination status: what the log says about a rejected step and the end of a run (`apply_redo`) {#sec-ch13-redo-view}

### Summary

When a step goes wrong, snapy throws it away and tries again with a smaller step. This section explains what the
log says when that happens, and what it says when a run ends, so a user can tell a normal stop from a failure.
How a step is accepted or rejected (the six causes, the collective decision, the halving and the restore) is
@sec-ch07-redo.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Prints the causes of every rejected step, and at the end why the run stopped, with exit status 1 if abnormal.

**Data.** Reads the globally reduced cause mask, the redo count and the stop reasons; writes log lines and the status.

**Placement.** `MeshBlockImpl::apply_redo` after each redo decision; `MeshBlockImpl::finalize` at the end of the run.

**Activation.** Always; the limits are `integration/tlim`, `nlim` and pyharp's `max_redo` (default 5, not a YAML key).

**Guarantee / limits.** Each list decodes to its mask; names the causes, not the cells or ranks that raised them.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer below, @tbl-ch13-redo-view-tests.
:::

Local symbols: none. The section names the cause bits in the text and uses no mathematical symbol.

### Derivation

There is nothing to derive; the section states how the log encodes the decision. Why each printed list identifies
its mask, in three steps:

1. *One name per bit.* `apply_redo` prints `floor`, `clamp`, `limiter`, `nan`, `saturation` and `vic-solve` for the
   bits 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 and 32 of the mask, each only when its bit is set.
2. *A fixed order.* The names are written in bit order, so a set of bits has one spelling.
3. *Hence the list decodes back to the mask*, and the 63 nonzero masks give 63 different lists (`[C1]`). The logic is
   on integers, so there is no round-off. A rejected step prints
`Redoing the step with smaller dt (causes: ...)`. The list names each set bit of the globally reduced cause mask
once, in bit order: `floor` (1), `clamp` (2), `limiter` (4), `nan` (8), `saturation` (16), `vic-solve` (32). The 63
nonzero masks print 63 different lists, and each list decodes back to its mask; mask 37 prints
`floor limiter vic-solve` [check `src/snapy_report/ch13/checks/redo_view_check.py`, output `redo_view_check.out`, `[C1]`].
When the redo count passes `max_redo`, the run ends with "Maximum number of redo attempts exceeded. Terminating."
If `vic-solve` is among the causes, the message adds "after restoring the rejected VIC step input" (`[C2]`).

At the end, `finalize` prints the first reason that holds, in this order: a terminate signal, an interrupt, the
wall-time alarm, the cycle limit `nlim` (when it is not negative) and the time limit `tlim`. If none holds it
prints "Terminating abnormally" and returns 1. Of the 32 combinations of the five reasons, only the empty one
returns 1 (`[C3]`).

See @sec-ch07-redo for redo / rollback. `apply_redo` prints the cause list and the two terminal messages
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::apply_redo >}}). `finalize` writes the final
output, prints the stop reason with the final `time`, `cycle`, `tlim` and `nlim`, and returns the status
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::finalize >}}). The example driver returns that status from `main` as `status`, so a shell
or a test harness sees it as the exit code ({{< code examples/run_hydro.cpp main >}}).

### Code

**A minimal input.** The stop reasons come from the integration block:

```yaml
integration:
  tlim: 600.     # stop at this time
  nlim: 200      # or after this many cycles; -1 (the default) disables it
```

`max_redo` is not a key of the card: pyharp's `from_yaml` reads only `type`, `cfl`, `tlim`, `nlim`, `ncycle_out` and
`verbose` ([`pyharp integrator.cpp:24-29`](https://github.com/chengcli/pyharp/blob/4721715855e937c1e8b218e964c0655f46e56e29/src/integrator/integrator.cpp#L24-L29)).
It keeps its default 5 unless set from code with `op.intg().max_redo(n)` before the block is built (@sec-ch10-redo).

**What is refused, and why.** A `max_redo` key in `integration`, which stops the run at construction with
"unknown key 'integration/max_redo'. Valid keys: implicit-scheme, implicit-advection-cfl, shear-cfl; read by pyharp:
type, cfl, tlim, nlim, ncycle_out, verbose." (`check_keys`,
{{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitOptionsImpl::from_yaml overload=1 >}}). At run time the run stops
past `max_redo` redos with "Maximum number of redo attempts exceeded. Terminating." (`[C2]`).

**The code, mapped to the log** ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::apply_redo >}}):

```cpp
<< (causes & 1 ? " floor" : "") << (causes & 2 ? " clamp" : "")
<< (causes & 4 ? " limiter" : "") << (causes & 8 ? " nan" : "")
<< (causes & 16 ? " saturation" : "")
<< (causes & 32 ? " vic-solve" : "") << ")." << std::endl;
```

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| local flags | {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::local_redo_flags >}} | `local_redo_flags` | |
| mask | {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::reduce_redo_flags >}} | `reduce_redo_flags` | |
| cause list, terminal messages | {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::apply_redo >}} | `apply_redo` | `max_redo` |
| Mesh flags | {{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::check_redo >}} | `local_redo_flag_tensor` | |
| stop reason and status | {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::finalize >}} | `finalize` | `tlim`, `nlim` |

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
The log names the causes but not the cells or the rank that raised them; the MAX reduction keeps only whether
any rank did. Only a VIC refusal prints its column, rank, step, stage and retry (@sec-ch07-vic-reject).
:::

1. **No count.** No meter counts the redos of a run; the count is the number of "Redoing" lines in the log.
2. **Single-block signals.** Only the Mesh path checks signals before the redo decision (@sec-ch07-redo).
3. **Untested combinations.** The switch combinations that a test exercises are listed in @sec-ch12-matrix.
